cells.quote: An examination of the age distribution shows the greatest progress between the six- and seven-year-olds (excepting the two cases 17 years old). The age progress is steady up to 14, when there is a slight drop, and another drop is shown by the four cases of 16 years.

D.comparison: grading by the single judge who rated all specimens

O.outcome_detail: agreement and deviations in handwriting ratings

result.effect: average deviation among eight judges 6.1; single judge deviation from their average 4.8

cells.quote: Since the specimens on the standard Ayres scale are placed 10 points apart, i. e., 20, 30, 40 90, it is significant that in every case but one the average of the deviations of the eight judges is below 10 and the average, of these average deviations is only 6.1. This seems to indicate that, while it is impossible to eliminate entirely the subjective factors in judging hand- writing, it may be reduced to a small quantity in the use of this scale.
cells.note: The reliability substudy used 34 specimens taken at random and graded independently by eight competent judges; the text presents agreement as evidence that the scale reduces subjectivity.

result.effect: 13-point gain from 1A to 2B; printed grade ranks rise from 22 in 1A to 59 in 8B

cells.quote: A number of interesting points may be noted in these results. For example, it is evident that a single judge can ap7)ly the scale with a fair degree of consistency, as is shown by the steady improvement manifest in the various grades from the 1st to 8B. The grades 5B, 5A and 6B are the only exceptions. Of these, 5B shows the only marked deviation from the upward trend.
cells.note: The comparison is across naturally occurring grades, not an intervention.

result.effect: mean rank rises from 28 at age 6 to 54 at age 14

cells.quote: An examination of the age distribution shows the greatest progress between the six- and seven-year-olds (excepting the two cases 17 years old). The age progress is steady up to 14, when there is a slight drop, and another drop is shown by the four cases of 16 years.
cells.note: The study cautions that results beyond age 15 are based on very few cases.

result.effect: School C average 45 versus School E average 37

cells.quote: It will be noted that the six elementary schools rank fairly close together. School E, which ranks the lowest, 37, contains pupils up to the 4B only. School C, which ranks highest, has small 6th and 7th grade classes.
cells.note: School differences are confounded by differing grade composition; the text specifically notes that School C's upper grades had negative deviations from its school average.

result.effect: average deviation of single judge from eight-judge average: 4.8

cells.quote: It is significant also to note that the deviations from these average rankings of the judge who ranked all the 966 specimens is not large, his average deviation being only 4.8, indicating that the ranking of the entire set of 966 by eight judges would not have differed markedly from the ranks assigned by this single judge.
cells.note: This is an inter-rater agreement comparison, not a randomized instructional contrast.
